Create ONE file and modify ONE file:
  1. api/_lib/resources/dutMap.js      (new)
  2. api/_lib/router.js                (add the routes)

Read these first and follow them exactly: api/_lib/resources/devices.js (or the closest existing
resource) for structure, api/_lib/router.js for how routes are registered, api/_lib/auth.js for how
the principal arrives, api/_lib/respond.js for the response envelope, and api/_lib/validate.js for
input validation. Match the existing files; do not introduce a new pattern.

WHAT IT IS FOR. `vault.dut_sample_map` already exists in the database (created by migration 0108
and referenced by 0114). It maps a bench DUT identifier such as `2kb-dut-01` to a vault sample id,
which is a registry key. They are UNRELATED NAMESPACES: deriving one from the other works for
today's names and silently misattributes measurements the first time a board is named differently.
cli/import_dut_map.py is written and blocked solely because no route reads or writes this table.

Routes to add:
  GET    /api/bench/dut-map           list all mappings
  GET    /api/bench/dut-map/:dutId    one mapping, 404 if absent
  PUT    /api/bench/dut-map/:dutId    create or update one mapping

Non-negotiable, each for a stated reason:
* PUT must REFUSE to change an existing mapping to a different sample_id unless the request
  explicitly opts in (a body flag, name it `allow_remap`). Re-pointing a dut_id silently
  re-attributes every measurement already registered through it. The refusal must say what it
  refused and what to pass.
* The provenance field is REQUIRED on create. A mapping with no stated basis -- a board label, a
  fab record, a notebook entry -- is a guess somebody wrote down, and it will be read later as
  fact. Reject a create without it.
* Admin-gated for writes, exactly the way the other resources gate admin actions. Reads follow the
  same rule as other read routes.
* Validate `dutId` against injection the same way the existing resources do. Do not hand-roll a new
  escaping scheme; use what api/_lib/query.js or validate.js already provides.

Then create tests/api-dutMap.test.ts, mirroring an existing tests/api-*.test.ts (they vi.mock
`supabaseAdmin` -- use the same mechanism, do not invent another). Cover: list, get-one, 404 for
unknown, create, the remap refusal, and the missing-provenance refusal.

Run `npx vitest run tests/api-dutMap.test.ts` and `node --check api/_lib/resources/dutMap.js
api/_lib/router.js` until green.

Create exactly ONE new file:
  1. tests/vaultApiServer.test.ts

A vitest suite over server/vault-api.mjs, which is the long-lived HTTP server that runs the same
api/handler.js the Vercel function ran. Read server/vault-api.mjs and scripts/api-dev.mjs first,
and read two existing tests in tests/ to match style.

Pin these, each a real hazard recorded in this repo's own notes:

1. IT MUST NOT ACCUMULATE REQUEST BODIES AS A STRING. scripts/api-dev.mjs does `raw += chunk`,
   which corrupts binary and reads a whole upload into memory. vault-api.mjs is the production
   server and the /content routes must stream. Assert the file does not contain a string
   accumulation of the request body, and that the content routes are handled by a streaming path.
   If vault-api.mjs DOES still accumulate, that is a real finding -- leave the assertion failing and
   say so; do not edit the server.

2. IT MUST BIND LOOPBACK. The server sits behind nginx and Caddy; binding a routable address would
   put the API on the network with its own credentials. Assert 127.0.0.1 and that 0.0.0.0 does not
   appear as a bind host.

3. EVERY process.env IT READS MUST BE DOCUMENTED. tests/envVarParity.test.ts already enforces this
   repo-wide; do not duplicate it. Instead assert the specific pair that drifted before: the server
   reads VAULT_REST_URL and VAULT_SERVICE_JWT and fails loudly if either is unset, rather than
   starting and 500ing on first request. A server that starts without credentials looks healthy to
   systemd and to a monitor.

4. Assert the file exists and exceeds a minimum size, in its own `it`. Every check above is a text
   search, and a text search over a missing or empty file passes while verifying nothing.

Include an `it` proving each detector fires against a small inline string containing the bad form.
Run `npx vitest run tests/vaultApiServer.test.ts` until green.

Create exactly ONE new file:
  1. scripts/migrate-vault-data.mjs

Copies the vault's rows and objects from the hosted Supabase project into the self-hosted endpoint.
Read cli/vault.py, api/_lib/supabaseAdmin.js and docs/CONNECT_INTERFACE.md first for the wire
shapes. Node ESM, no new dependencies -- use global fetch.

Source and destination both come from the environment; NEVER hardcode a URL or a key:
  SOURCE_REST_URL / SOURCE_SERVICE_KEY   (hosted Supabase)
  VAULT_REST_URL  / VAULT_SERVICE_JWT    (self-hosted, already used by this repo)
  SOURCE_STORAGE_URL / VAULT_STORAGE_URL for objects

THE RULES, each with its reason kept as a comment:

* BLOBS FIRST, NEVER ROWS FIRST. Blobs-first can only leave an object with no row, which is
  classifiable and fixed by re-running. Rows-first leaves a row pointing at an object that does not
  exist -- an entry nobody can interpret later and which every consumer treats as corruption.
* KEYSET PAGING, never offset. `id=gt.<last>` ordered by id. Offset paging against a table
  receiving inserts SKIPS rows silently, and a migration that silently skips rows is worse than one
  that fails.
* Verify each object by sha256 after transfer, and compare against the row's recorded hash where
  one exists. Re-download rather than trust a matching SIZE: a truncated-then-resumed transfer that
  lands on the same length is invisible to a size check.
* IDEMPOTENT AND RESUMABLE. Record progress to a state file so an interrupted run continues rather
  than restarting. Re-running a completed migration must be a no-op that says so.
* `--dry-run` is the default first step and must write NOTHING anywhere. Say so in --help.
* NEVER delete or modify anything at the source. The hosted projects remain the system of record
  until something else has demonstrably replaced them. Make that structural: no DELETE or PATCH
  against SOURCE_*, ever.
* Exit non-zero on any failure and print a per-table summary of copied / skipped / failed.

Known-bad rows to expect and classify rather than crash on: `files` rows stuck in a pending or
failed upload state from abandoned flows, and rows whose sha256 is null -- null is distinct in a
unique constraint, so duplicates are possible. Report them; do not silently drop them.

Run `node --check scripts/migrate-vault-data.mjs` before finishing.

  1. .env.example
  2. docs/DEPLOY_CHECKLIST.md   (only the vault-api environment section)

server/vault-api.mjs and api/_lib/* read exactly these from the environment:
  VAULT_REST_URL, VAULT_SERVICE_JWT, VAULT_STORAGE_URL, VAULT_API_KEY,
  VAULT_ACCESS_TEAM_URL, VAULT_ACCESS_AUD, VAULT_EMAIL_DOMAIN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, PORT

Make sure every one is documented with what it is for and what breaks without it, and that nothing
is documented which the code does not read.

THIS IS ENFORCED BY A TEST. tests/envVarParity.test.ts fails the build in BOTH directions: a
variable read but undocumented, and -- the one that matters more -- a variable documented but never
read. The second is the silent failure: an operator sets it, believes the feature is configured,
and it is not. That test exists because VAULT_IDENTITY_* was documented in four files and read by
none. Run `npx vitest run tests/envVarParity.test.ts` after your edit and make sure it still passes.

Concrete facts for the values on the live host:
  VAULT_REST_URL     http://127.0.0.1:8087/rest/v1
  VAULT_STORAGE_URL  http://127.0.0.1:8087/storage/v1
  PORT               8099   (NOT 3001, which fed_storage owns on this host)
  VAULT_SERVICE_JWT  an HS256 token with role vault_service, signed with the shared secret in
                     the server's secrets.env. That secret must never be regenerated: PostgREST and
                     fed_storage verify the same tokens with it, so a new one gives working metadata
                     reads and 401 on every object download, which reads as a corrupt archive.
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY  server-side only, for the search agent. It must never reach a browser.

Do not modify any other file.
